profile.reading: This registry row's operator field was corrected from Equinix to Digital Fortress in an earlier pass, after this facility was divested by Equinix to Chirisa Investments in 2019 and rebranded as Digital Fortress Piscataway; Equinix is retained as former_operator per this registry's no deletion policy. Digital Fortress's own current page for this facility, fetched fresh, gives the address 201B Centennial Avenue, Piscataway Township, New Jersey, and describes a 96,500 square foot building comprising 9,700 square feet of built out white space and 14,000 square feet of shell space available for future buildout, with 1.8 megawatts of UPS power capacity in an N+1 configuration, up to 15 kilowatts per cabinet available without significant redesign, and 800 tons of chilled water cooling capacity. The operator's own page lists SOC I and SOC II Type II compliance, supporting PCI and HIPAA frameworks, along with 24 by 7 network operations center monitoring, key card access, slab on grade concrete construction, and a 48 inch raised floor with underfloor leak and smoke detection. Digital Fortress, per trade press coverage on this registry's separate Meadowville, Virginia row, has operated since 1994, growing from nine facilities nationwide as a multi tenant and wholesale data center provider serving enterprises across multiple states including New Jersey, Virginia, Washington, Oregon, Colorado, and Illinois, and is a Chirisa Investments portfolio company. Baxtel and other aggregators independently corroborate this same address and the operator's current Digital Fortress branding at this building. Piscataway Township sits in Middlesex County, New Jersey, within the broader New York and New Jersey data center corridor that also hosts major Equinix, Digital Realty, and CoreSite campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry, drawing colocation demand from proximity to Manhattan financial and media firms at lower New Jersey real estate and power costs. The buildings continued use as a data center facility across two different operators, first Equinix and now Digital Fortress, reflects a broader industry pattern in which purpose built colocation real estate tends to remain in data center use through ownership changes given the high cost and long lead time of new construction relative to acquiring and rebranding an existing facility.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This registry row lists operator Equinix, but this session finds that attribution is stale. Per Baxtel trade press coverage, this facility was previously acquired by Equinix in May 2017 as part of a large 28 data center deal with Verizon, and operated as Equinix NY12. Per that same Baxtel coverage, Equinix subsequently divested this specific Piscataway, New Jersey facility to Chirisa Investments, with the acquisition closing in Fall 2019, after which the facility was rebranded Digital Fortress Piscataway, run by Digital Fortress, a Chirisa portfolio company. This session independently corroborates the change is current, not just historical, via Digital Fortress own current site, a tier-1 operator source, which describes operating a 96,500 square foot Piscataway, New Jersey facility, closely matching Baxtels reported 96,559 square feet for the former Equinix NY12 building, and via independent Data Center Dynamics trade press coverage of Chirisa acquiring this and other former Equinix facilities. Aggregators datacenterHawk and DataCenterMap have likewise updated their own listings to Digital Fortress branding at this same address. One aggregator, Datacenters.com, was found this session still presenting a stale listing under the old Equinix NY12 branding, with no mention of the ownership change, flagged here as an outdated source rather than treated as current. Given this weight of tier-1 and independent trade press evidence, this session updates the operator field on this row from Equinix to Digital Fortress, recording Equinix as former_operator rather than deleting the prior attribution, per this registrys standard policy for ownership changes. The facility address itself, per Digital Fortress own site and corroborating aggregators, is 201B Centennial Avenue, Piscataway Township, NJ. reading.body:
This 96,500 square foot facility in Piscataway Township publishes 1.8 megawatts of IT load in an N+1 UPS configuration, with 9,700 square feet of built white space and 14,000 square feet of shell space available for expansion. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 1.8 megawatts of IT load represents roughly 45 racks. The operator publishes support for up to 15 kilowatts per cabinet without significant redesign, and 800 tons of chilled water cooling capacity.

The facility holds SOC I and SOC II Type II compliance supporting PCI and HIPAA frameworks, qualifying it for regulated enterprise and financial workloads. It sits in Middlesex County, New Jersey, the sixth-ranked facility by published capacity in a state of 48 mapped data center sites, where only five facilities publish power specifications and the total published capacity across all mapped sites is 111.3 megawatts. The facility is part of the New York and New Jersey data center corridor serving colocation demand from proximity to Manhattan financial and media firms at lower New Jersey real estate and power costs.

The building was divested by Equinix to Chirisa Investments in 2019 and now operates under the Digital Fortress brand. Digital Fortress has operated since 1994 across nine facilities nationwide as a multi-tenant and wholesale data center provider. The 201B Centennial Avenue address reflects a broader industry pattern in which purpose-built colocation real estate tends to remain in data center use through ownership changes given the high cost and long lead time of new construction relative to acquiring and rebranding an existing facility. Power specification publication is the exception rather than the rule in New Jersey, making this disclosed capacity a data point in a sparse landscape.
